raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

FastH3 8-Step V2 was distilled with VSA-H3 (`fastvideo_inference.json`: `attention_backend: VIDEO_SPARSE_ATTN_H3`, `vsa_sparsity: 0.8`). Since #37662, sglang runs VSA-H3 only when it is selected with `--component-attention-backends transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3`. A FastH3 server started without it serves dense FlashAttention: the trained `to_gate_compress` branch is skipped, and on 4x H200 a request takes 12.6 s instead of 10.0 s.

That is easy to miss. Our cross-framework benchmark profile predated #37662 (#41839 selected VSA-H3 itself) and ran dense attention for three days, while vLLM-Omni served the same checkpoint with VSA. sglang went from ahead to 15% behind on H200, and the server log only says `Using fa attention backend`.

## Modifications

- `FastH3PipelineConfig.validate_server_args` selects `video_sparse_attn_h3` for the transformer when the user gave no transformer backend (neither `--attention-backend` nor a transformer entry in `--component-attention-backends`). The text encoder and VAEs keep their own backends, as the cookbook recommends.
- It does not select it, and dense attention stays, where VSA-H3 cannot run: off CUDA, on GPUs other than SM90 / SM100 / SM103 (the backend's supported set, now `VSA_H3_CAPABILITIES` in `platforms/cuda.py`), or with torch.compile, the breakable CUDA graph or ring attention, which VSA-H3 rejects.
- `ServerArgs.set_automatic_component_attention_backend` records the choice as automatic (`is_component_attention_backend_automatic`), the same way LTX-2 records its text-encoder backend.
- Cookbook: describe the default and how to select dense attention (`--component-attention-backends transformer=fa`).

## Accuracy Tests

With no transformer backend given, the default now goes through the same path as passing `--component-attention-backends transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3` explicitly. Nothing changes when a backend is given.

4x H200, base `53295c697` (main) vs this branch (`f6f923520`), the FastH3 V2 T2VA request (1344x768, 124 frames, seed 1101, 8 steps), two requests per server, MP4 md5 of each request:

| server | transformer backend | md5 (request 1 / 2) |
|---|---|---|
| main, no transformer backend | `fa` | `25b927f2` / `9de1795b` |
| **this PR, no transformer backend** | `video_sparse_attn_h3` (automatic) | **`4a7fb255` / `e62efe95`** |
| this PR, `--component-attention-backends transformer=fa` | `fa` | `25b927f2` / `9de1795b` |
| main, `--component-attention-backends transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3` | `video_sparse_attn_h3` | `4a7fb255` / `e62efe95` |

The new default matches the explicit VSA-H3 flag bit for bit, and an explicit `fa` still matches main's dense output bit for bit. Both rounds gave the same md5s.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Same box, the four servers interleaved twice, client wall clock per request (median of two after warmup), sglang eager (`--ulysses-degree 4 --performance-mode speed --enable-torch-compile false`):

| server | round 1 (s) | round 2 (s) |
|---|---:|---:|
| main, no transformer backend (dense FA) | 12.656 | 12.639 |
| **this PR, no transformer backend** | **10.064** | **10.027** |
| this PR, `transformer=fa` | 12.646 | 12.706 |
| main, `transformer=video_sparse_attn_h3` | 10.053 | 9.994 |

On this box vLLM-Omni eager serves the same checkpoint with VSA in 10.95–11.06 s.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit.
- [x] Unit tests: `test_server_args.py` (default on SM90 / SM100 / SM103; kept dense for an explicit transformer backend, an explicit `--attention-backend`, torch.compile, and SM80) and `test_minimax_h3_fasth3.py`.
- [x] Docs: cookbook FastH3 section.

@@ -904,9 +904,14 @@ refiner falls back to dense FA inside the backend, and the text encoder and
 VAEs keep their own backends. Ulysses sequence parallelism is supported. See
 [Attention Backends](/docs/sglang-diffusion/attention_backends) for
 `VSA_sparsity`, `vsa_mode`, `vsa_dense_first_n_steps`, and
-`vsa_dense_layers`. Every dense backend that runs on base H3 (`fa`,
-`torch_sdpa`, ...) also runs on the FastH3 weights without VSA flags, and
-`sglang generate` takes the same flags as `sglang serve`.
+`vsa_dense_layers`. On CUDA, FastH3 selects VSA-H3 for the transformer when no
+transformer backend is given, unless torch.compile, the breakable CUDA graph or
+ring attention is on (VSA-H3 serves none of them). Every dense backend that
+runs on base H3 also runs on the FastH3 weights, without the compression
+branch: select it with `--component-attention-backends transformer=fa` (or
+`torch_sdpa`, ...). On 4× H200 dense FA is about 25% slower end to end than
+VSA-H3 (12.6 s against 10.0 s). `sglang generate` takes the same flags as
+`sglang serve`.
 
 Measured latencies for the 4× GB300 recipe are in
 [FastH3 on GB300](#fasth3-on-gb300).

@@ -28,6 +28,9 @@
     AttentionBackendEnum,
     current_platform,
 )
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.utils.logging_utils import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
 
 
 @dataclass
@@ -355,8 +358,43 @@ def validate_server_args(self, server_args) -> None:
                 "--model-variant does not apply. FL2VA and Ref2VA tasks were "
                 "not distilled; use MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 for those."
             )
+        self._default_to_trained_sparse_attention(server_args)
         super().validate_server_args(server_args)
 
+    def _default_to_trained_sparse_attention(self, server_args) -> None:
+        # The checkpoint was distilled with VSA-H3; dense attention skips its
+        # trained compression gate and runs slower.
+        if self.resolve_transformer_attention_backend(server_args) is not None:
+            return
+        if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+            return
+        from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.platforms.cuda import VSA_H3_CAPABILITIES
+
+        capability = current_platform.get_device_capability()
+        if (
+            capability is None
+            or (capability.major, capability.minor) not in VSA_H3_CAPABILITIES
+        ):
+            return
+        if (
+            server_args.enable_torch_compile
+            or server_args.enable_breakable_cuda_graph
+            or int(server_args.ring_degree or 1) > 1
+        ):
+            logger.info(
+                "FastH3 runs dense attention: VSA-H3 does not serve torch.compile, "
+                "the breakable CUDA graph or ring attention"
+            )
+            return
+        server_args.set_automatic_component_attention_backend(
+            "transformer", AttentionBackendEnum.VIDEO_SPARSE_ATTN_H3.name.lower()
+        )
+        logger.info(
+            "Automatically set video_sparse_attn_h3 for the FastH3 transformer, the "
+            "attention it was distilled with; --component-attention-backends "
+            "transformer=fa selects dense attention"
+        )
+
 
 __all__ = ["FastH3PipelineConfig", "MiniMaxH3PipelineConfig"]

+# The vendored Triton tile-64 kernel is written against Hopper and Blackwell

+VSA_H3_CAPABILITIES = frozenset({(9, 0), (10, 0), (10, 3)})
+
+
 class _VideoSparseAttentionH3BackendResolver(_CudaAttentionBackendResolver):
     backend = AttentionBackendEnum.VIDEO_SPARSE_ATTN_H3
-

+    supported_capabilities = VSA_H3_CAPABILITIES
 
     @classmethod
     def resolve(cls, platform) -> str:

+            return _from_dict_without_model_resolution(

+    def test_fasth3_selects_vsa_h3_for_the_transformer(self):
+        for capability in ((9, 0), (10, 0), (10, 3)):
+            with self.subTest(capability=capability):
+                args = self._fasth3_args(capability)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    args.component_attention_backends,

+                self.assertTrue(
